course_summary:
ISEN 635 | Human Information Processing | Fall 2025
Instructor: Thomas Ferris | tferris@tamu.edu
Meets: Tuesdays, 5:30 PM - 8:00 PM | ZACH 361
Grading: Homework [30%], Exams [50%], Semester project [20%] — A: 90-100%, B: 80-89%, D: 60-69%, F: 59% and lower
Topics: neuropsychological processes, human-systems analysis and design methods, neuroanatomy, sensory physiology, cognitive systems engineering, psychophysiological methods, signal detection theory, information theory, mental workload assessment, user-centered design principles, Psychophysics, Vigilance, color vision, object recognition, depth perception, Audition, Timesharing, Assessing mental workload, Haptics, haptic communication, Multisensory processing, Multimodal interfaces, human information processing, models of basic cognitive functions, pattern recognition, attention, memory, cognitive psychology, philosophy, communication skills, quantitative problem exercises, reading responses, engineering analyses, redesign solutions, Sensation & Perception, Visual processing, Attention in visual processing, Learning, Design for supporting Human Information Processing, Usability, interaction
Tools: Canvas, Zoom
